prompt:
Create a new KFB claymation ink blob sheet, The Practice Rooms. Use the original reference PNGs for the established organic full-body ink monster morphology and modeling. Exactly six whole independent standalone dark charcoal-plum goo figures, three columns and two rows, landscape 1536×1024 true transparent PNG. Every face is sculpted directly into its continuous organic blob. Think six different compact asymmetrical drips, rounded pears, commas and irregular splats, as varied as the original family. Maintain each individual silhouette, with natural soft little lobes at the sides and bottom, sometimes no distinct foot shape. A short round or tapered bottom is welcome. Do not use a standard flared base, wide flat skirt, common lobe row, humanoid chest or cut-off bust. Clothing is just a small removable accessory and props sit close to the side or belly with the lower body visible. Thick sculpted dark lids, white sclera, red iris and black pupil. Soft satin clay, sparse broad hand modeling marks, distinct moods, tiny ink hands. No inherited costume, wing or eyepatch, scenery, floor, shadow, frame or text beyond specified prop marks. Preserve generous transparent separation and exterior margin. Terracotta, ultramarine, muted yellow and apricot. Tiny removable outfit accents.
Row-major roles:
1. Male-read art teacher. wide undulating splat, elated uneven smile. Key cue: small paint palette with three smooth color dabs and stubby brush.
2. Female-read music teacher. tall soft pear, eyebrow raised, rhythmic closed smile. Key cue: small metronome with a chunky swinging arm.
3. Male-read drama teacher. curved asymmetrical blob, cheeky side-eye. Key cue: single hand-held half mask with a raised eyebrow, real face visible.
4. Female-read physical education teacher. compact broad blob, lively direct eyes and determined grin. Key cue: short relay baton and one small stopwatch.
5. Male-read home economics teacher. rounded low square, proud quiet smile. Key cue: small mixing bowl with a rising lump and blunt wooden spoon.
6. Male-read craft teacher. upright bent oval, focused downcast eyes. Key cue: one pair of oversized wooden dovetail pieces fitted partway together.
Each actor has a distinct complete compact ink contour from crown to lower edge and one clean readable subject or role prop.
